tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: The one yearly goal: kind (count or done), metric, starting value, current value, target, deadline, progress, levers (hard/comfortable) and other projects. Call first in most flows.

tools.name: check_goal_draft
tools.description: Check a goal that is not saved yet against the rubric (a countable metric with value today and target, or a done-or-not result you can check yes or no; deadline within 12 months; pace per week). Changes nothing. Returns problems[] and next_question: loop until problems is empty, then call set_goal.

tools.name: set_goal
tools.description: Save the yearly goal, or replace it with the next one. Rejects with problems[] if the rubric fails. Keeps levers and projects. area is which of the five life areas the goal belongs to.

tools.name: record_progress
tools.description: Record the current value of the goal metric ("I now have 4 customers"), or of a countable milestone when milestoneId is given ("I have talked to 7 people"). For a done-or-not goal, 1 marks it done. One value per date: calling again for the same date corrects it. Says when the target is reached; a co

tools.name: set_levers
tools.description: Replace the list of levers: the recurring kinds of goal work. At least one must be kind=hard (the work the user avoids). keywords/repos are hints for classifying sessions from their task text. Pass existing ids to keep them.

tools.name: set_projects
tools.description: Replace the list of other projects (paid work, other products, life routines), so their sessions count as other work or life, not goal work. Pass the whole list: leave one out to remove it, change its name or hints to edit it. Pass existing ids to keep them.

tools.name: get_path
tools.description: Milestones with kind, progress (recorded value or steps done), pace (ahead/on_pace/behind) and their steps. current_milestone_id is the one to work on.

tools.name: set_milestones
tools.description: Replace the list of 2–6 ordered milestones under the goal, each countable (metric and target) or measured by its steps, with a due date before the goal deadline. Pass each existing id, or that milestone's steps are deleted. To change one milestone, use edit_milestone.

tools.name: edit_milestone
tools.description: Change one milestone: title, kind (count or steps), metric, target, due date or status. status=retired drops it without finishing; done or retired moves the path to the next milestone. Its steps are kept.

tools.name: add_steps
tools.description: Add concrete steps to a milestone. A step is an action that fits a few work blocks ("email 10 people from the waitlist"), not "do marketing". Abstract steps are rejected. Put a hard-lever step first; preparation only where it blocks it (warns otherwise).

tools.name: edit_step
tools.description: Change one step: title, status (todo/doing/done), order, lever, estimate.

tools.name: delete_step
tools.description: Delete one step from the path.

tools.name: next_steps
tools.description: Open steps of the current milestone, hard-lever steps first: the candidates for today's main step.

tools.name: get_commitments
tools.description: Recurring weekly time: commitments (school runs, training, classes), overhead (sleep, meals) and focus windows.

tools.name: set_commitments
tools.description: Replace the list of recurring weekly commitments. days are ISO weekdays 1=Mon..7=Sun; use timesPerWeek instead when there are no fixed days. Pass existing ids to keep them.

tools.name: get_capacity
tools.description: Weekly time budget out of 168 hours: overhead, hours committed per area, focus windows, and what is still unaccounted for. Nothing is assumed.

tools.name: get_planning_context
tools.description: Everything needed to plan a day: goal and pace, next_steps, yesterday's summary and undone items, week balance, days since a hard lever. Defaults to tomorrow. The agent plans; then call set_plan.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: The plan for a day (default today).

tools.name: set_plan
tools.description: Replace the plan for a day. Exactly one item must have isMainStep=true (the step toward the goal), ideally linked by stepId from next_steps and on a hard lever. Warns when no item is on a hard lever. Other items: paid work, family, workout, etc. with their area. Items that stay keep their done state

tools.name: edit_plan_item
tools.description: Change one plan item: mark it done or not done, rename it, change its estimate, area or links, or make it the main step. done=true also completes its linked path step. For a weekly routine, count says how many units this tick did (talked to 2 people today). For a routine, level minimum says only its

tools.name: get_routines
tools.description: Routines: small steps that repeat on fixed weekdays, e.g. "talk with one person on Reddit", or that count up to a number a week, e.g. "talk to 5 people a week", each with an optional bad-day minimum. The server adds them to each matching day's plan, so every device and agent sees the same checks. Wi

tools.name: set_routines
tools.description: Replace the list of routines: small steps that repeat on fixed weekdays. From today on, each one appears as a plan item on its days; tick it with edit_plan_item, skip it for one day with delete_plan_item. set_plan keeps them. days are ISO weekdays 1=Mon..7=Sun, default every day. perWeek makes it a

tools.name: delete_plan_item
tools.description: Remove one item from a day's plan. A routine item is skipped for that day only.

tools.name: set_day_mode
tools.description: Tracking for a day: full (everything recorded, the default) or off (timer and reminders only, nothing stored, no plan required).

tools.name: get_now
tools.description: What is happening now: running sessions with attention shares, the timer, today's main step, today's minutes, the streak and a one-line nudge.

tools.name: start_session
tools.description: Start a session of work and, if none is running, the timer. Returns a verdict: ok | stop | plan_first. On "stop" NO session is created: relay the message, ask the user; if they insist, call again with override=true. Several sessions may run at once (two terminals) and share attention by weight. Apps

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Add a one-line note to a running session (this connection's, or session_id). May classify a session that was unclassified.

tools.name: split_attention
tools.description: Set attention weights of the running sessions at once, e.g. {"abc": 0.7, "def": 0.3}. Applies to the whole session. For a finished session use edit_session.

tools.name: stop_session
tools.description: Stop a running session with a summary and outcome. Pass session_id from get_now; without it, only this connection's single running session is stopped, never another one. The timer keeps running for other sessions. outcome=done completes the linked plan item or path step. Without end_at or op_id it r

tools.name: stop_timer
tools.description: Stop the timer ("pause", "stop", "stand up") and every running session with it. There is no paused state: resuming starts a new session. Pass summary and outcome to save them on the sessions it closes, or call stop_session first. Returns the break length.

tools.name: add_session
tools.description: Add past time that was not timed: minutes (ending now, or at end), or start+end as HH:MM on date. For calls, children, workout, paid work, or work done away from the agent. Apps replaying a queued entry pass op_id, so a retry does not count the time twice.

tools.name: edit_session
tools.description: Fix a session, running or finished: start and end (HH:MM on date; an end before the start means it ran past midnight), task, area, project, lever, step, plan item, summary, outcome, attention share, weight. It is classified again after a change. Use it when a timer was forgotten or a session was lab

tools.name: delete_session
tools.description: Delete a session, running or finished, so it no longer counts. Pass session_id from get_now or list_sessions; without it, only this connection's single running session is deleted, never another one.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: Sessions in a date range (default the last 7 days), with ids, optionally filtered by area or project.

tools.name: find_gaps
tools.description: Untimed stretches of 20+ minutes between the first and last session of a day. Ask the user what happened there.

tools.name: summarize_day
tools.description: Full summary of a day: wall and attention minutes per area, classification and lever, sessions, gaps, overlaps, overrides.

tools.name: summarize_week
tools.description: A week, Monday to Sunday (to today for the current week): main-step days, goal share, hard share, area balance, overrides, streak, milestone pace.

tools.name: get_insights
tools.description: Week (the last 7 days) or month (the last 30 days) ending on to (default today): minutes per day on the aim, other work and life; hard vs comfortable share of aim time; an hour × weekday heatmap of aim minutes (6:00–23:00, Mon–Sun) with its hard part and the peak; main-step days; and comebacks (acti

tools.name: find_leaks
tools.description: Where time leaks: comfortable goal work while the main step waited, overrides, unplanned work, gaps, switching, missed main steps, days without a plan. Default the last 7 days.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: Timezone, where reminders go (desktop or mobile), timer settings, and which networks get progress posts (post_to).

tools.name: set_settings
tools.description: Change any of: timezone (IANA name, e.g. Europe/Madrid; it sets where each day starts and ends), workplace for reminders, stand-up interval workMin, breakMin, longBreakEvery, longBreakMin, standup on/off, post_to (networks for progress posts).

tools.name: add_device
tools.description: Register a device token so server reminders (stand up, break over) can reach it. The phone app registers itself; use this for testing or a manual token.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: Which devices can receive reminders, and when each was last seen.

tools.name: delete_device
tools.description: Remove a device so it stops receiving reminders.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: Agents connected to this AimYear account (Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, the AimYear app…): name, client_id, when it connected and when it was last active. current marks the one calling.

tools.name: delete_agent
tools.description: Disconnect one agent: its sign-in for this account is deleted and it can no longer read or change anything until it connects again. Only on the user's explicit request. client_id from list_agents.

tools.name: add_social_account
tools.description: Connect WIP (wip.co) or Bluesky so AimYear can post the day's progress there when the user says Post (Pro). WIP: api_key from wip.co settings. Bluesky: handle and an app password (Settings → Privacy and security → App passwords), never the account password. The login is checked, stored encrypted and

tools.name: list_social_accounts
tools.description: Connected networks (handle, since when), which of them get progress posts, and whether the user has Pro. Never returns any key or password.

tools.name: delete_social_account
tools.description: Disconnect a network and delete its saved login. Posts already made stay there.

tools.name: get_post_draft
tools.description: The day's progress post drafted from the record (aim and progress, main step done or not, minutes on the aim and on hard work, routines, comebacks), at most 300 characters, ending with aimyear.com; and per network whether it is ready, already posted, or skipped because the user already posted there

tools.name: add_post
tools.description: Post the day's progress, only after the user explicitly said to post. text is the draft as the user edited it (default: the draft from get_post_draft). Goes to the networks chosen in settings, or the ones given. A network where the user already posted that day themselves is skipped. Each day goes to

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: set_routines, get_settings, list_social_accounts, get_post_draft · Private data: record_progress, add_device, add_social_account, list_social_accounts, get_post_draft · Public sink: add_steps, start_session, edit_session, summarize_week, get_insights, add_social_account, get_post_draft, add_post · Destructive: set_projects, delete_step, delete_plan_item, start_session, delete_session, delete_device, delete_agent, delete_social_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: set_routines, get_settings, list_social_accounts, get_post_draft · Private data: record_progress, add_device, add_social_account, list_social_accounts, get_post_draft · Public sink: add_steps, start_session, edit_session, summarize_week, get_insights, add_social_account, get_post_draft, add_post · Destructive: set_projects, delete_step, delete_plan_item, start_session, delete_session, delete_device, delete_agent, delete_social_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
